surface_mechanism_description: During the ALD process, the surface reactions involve the formation of hydroxyl-terminated surfaces in H2O-based processes, where the concentration of surface hydroxyl groups depends on the crystallographic faces. In contrast, O3-based processes form oxygen-terminated surfaces, leading to different preferential growth directions. The hydroxyl groups determine the amount of metal precursor adsorbed during the subsequent metal precursor pulse, influencing the growth per cycle (GPC).
evidence: During the H2O pulse, a hydroxyl-terminated surface is formed in the H2O-based processes while the concentration of the surface hydroxyl groups can significantly depend on the crystallographic faces where they are formed. The concentration of hydroxyl groups determines, in turn, the amount of the metal adsorbed during the following metal precursor pulse. For this reason, GPC depends on the orientation of crystallites in the polycrystalline films and development of preferential orientation has been recorded with increasing thickness of oxide films grown in H2O-based ALD processes. During the O3 pulse, in contrast, oxygen-terminated surface is formed and, as can be concluded from the results of earlier studies, the preferential growth directions can markedly differ from those observed in the H2O-based processes.
